claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr lattice heat transport can be accurately predicted using ab initio molecular dynamics with explicit defect and impurity modeling.
HfNbTaTiZr electronic heat transport can be accurately predicted using ab initio molecular dynamics with explicit defect and impurity modeling.
Explicit modeling of defects and impurities will outperform earlier predictive approaches.
The improvement over earlier approaches will result from capturing atomic-scale complexity and the effects of defects and impurities.
The applicable material state is a bulk HfNbTaTiZr crystal containing potential defects and impurities.
A representative impurity level is 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed approach applies below 200 K.
The proposed approach applies from 300 to 1200 K.
Explicit consideration of defects and impurities in ab initio molecular dynamics captures the relevant atomic-scale complexity.
The proposed method could reduce prediction error by 20–30% relative to earlier approaches.
Measured total thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr from 300 to 1200 K is 10–17 W/(K m).
The predictions can be evaluated by comparing separately predicted lattice and electronic contributions with experimental measurements across varying defect and impurity concentrations.
Deviation of the predicted lattice and electronic contributions from experiment by more than 30% falsifies the hypothesis.
